FORM.AppraisalReportContentName: Market Conditions Addendum to the Appraisal Report

MARKET.SalesConcessionDescription: Seller contribution has been between 0% to 6%. No comparable adjustment was warranted for seller concessions.
MARKET.NeighborhoodMarketabilityFactorsDescript: There is a mixture of arms length transactions and foreclosures/short sales from banks in the area but they do not impact the marketability of the subject.
MARKET.DataSourceDescription: The data provided in this analysis was generated using the CVRMLS and county records.
MARKET.MarketTrendsReconciliationComment: This data and sample size is considered to be reliable and the amount of research to analyze this information is consistent with data located on on multiple listing service. This sample size used is similar multi-family properties fitting to the market consistency of the subject property. All data is within a 3 mile radius from subject inside and outside the neighborhood. The search excludes sub-market data and only uses closed sales and active listings. The results may vary from the top of page three do to a larger search of similar sales and actives outside the immediate neighborhood.

STRUCTURE.StructureConfigurationTypeOtherDescripti: None; No personal property was included in this appraisal.

SITE.HighestBestUseDescription: The best probable, financially feasible, physically possible, and legal use of the subject is the present use and results in the highest value.

NEIGHBORHOOD._BoundaryAndCharacteristicsDescription: Subject is bound by E Bank St to the North, N Old Church St to the East, Richmond-Petersburg Turnpike to the West, and Taylor St to the South.
NEIGHBORHOOD._MarketabilityFactorsDescription: Subject is located in the urban area of the City of Petersburg. No adverse conditions were noted to affect the neighborhood. The neighborhood has average convenience to amenities. Average quality single family homes are the predominant improvements. The appeal and marketability of properties in the subjects neighborhood are average for age and price range.

VALUATION_METHODS._AdditionalDescription:
Clarification of Intended Use and Intended User:
The Intended User of this appraisal report is the Lender/Client. The Intended Use is to evaluate the property that is the subject of this appraisal for a mortgage finance transaction, subject to the stated Scope of Work, purpose of the appraisal, reporting requirements of this appraisal report form, and Definition of Market Value. No additional Intended Users are identified by the appraiser.
This appraisal was prepared in accordance with the requirements of Title XI § 323.4 Minimum appraisal standards of the Financial Institutions, Reform, Recovery & Enforcement ACT (FIRREA) of 1989, as amended (12 U.S.C. 3331 et seq.), and any applicable implementing regulations in effect at the time the appraisal report was signed.
The appraiser was not influenced by any outside source and has reported credible results in this report.
"Other" land use reflects parks, recreational facilities, government and state owned properties.

COST_ANALYSIS.SiteEstimatedValueComment: Based on the application of the land to total assessed ratio of the assessor to the estimated market value for the subject, the subject’s site value is estimated at $40,000 or 28% of the subjects value. This site value is considered an assessed ratio value and is not a comparable sale derived value. Site values are similar across the board. No site adjustments were made.
COST_ANALYSIS._Comment: THE COST APPROACH IS DEVELOPED UTILIZING SWIFT ESTEMATOR. ESTIMATES ARE "REPLACEMENT" NOT REPRODUCTION COST. PHYSICAL DEPRECIATION IS CALCULATED USING THE EFFECTIVE AGE/LIFE METHOD.

SALES_COMPARISON._CurrentSalesAgreementAnalysisComment: The subject has not been transferred within the past three years. None of the comparables have been transferred within the past year.
SALES_COMPARISON._Comment: All comparables are located in the subject's market trend area and are of similar style, construction and utility. The chosen properties in this report are the most reflective of the subject. Net and gross adjustments are not always given equal weight. Appraiser further notes that most comparable adjustments were made on a case-by-case basis and not uniformly. Some adjustments were made relative to the appraisers experience and appraiser peers (through field reviews of appraiser peers) The appraiser further notes, any significant differences in the comparables relative to the subject were taken into consideration upon arriving at the Subject's opinion of value (i.e. GLA, room count, condition, build quality, location, etc). Conversely, there may be some differences that were not significant enough to consider for an adjustment.

INCOME_ANALYSIS._Comment: All rental information was confirmed with MLS data or management company. The leased amounts relative to market sales of comparable properties was the derivative to arriving at a value conclusion through the Income Approach. All comparables were weighted equally with respect to the GRM.

MULTIFAMILY_RENT_SCHEDULE.MarketRentalDataComment: The subject is rented for above market rent. Please analyze the rental comparables. The predominant market rent for the area is $.90 per sf. The appraiser notes that according to the market data in the MLS, the rent amounts are average amounts in the area. The rental properties are also in similar market condition as the subject. Upon net and gross adjustments to the leased comparables, the subjects opinion of market rent is warranted.

MULTIFAMILY_RENTALS.RentalDataAnalysisComment: Rent in the area appears to be from between $.75/sf to $1.00/sf in the market area. This data would include all styles of multi-family homes (duplex, quad, triplex, etc). The comparables above were pulled from the similar markets and support the subjects opinion of market rent. The appraiser notes that the market rent opinion is $0.90 per sf. The subject is in average rental condition (average rent amounts per the chosen leased comparables).

_RECONCILIATION._SummaryComment: Sales comparison is given most weight. Cost Approach is supportive of the value indication but less reliable because of estimations used for costs and depreciation. The Income Approach was also developed.
